Duterte Impeachment Stalls... A Report from China Daily by Prime Sarmiento..

The Philippine Senate’s handling of Vice-President Sara Duterte’s impeachment proceeding is testing the legislative body’s impartiality amid the “sharpening of elite political rivalries”, analysts said.

Anna Malindog-Uy, vice-president of the Asian Century Philippines Strategic Studies Institute, said Duterte’s impeachment is “a clear sign of the breakdown of the once-existing alliance” between the Duterte and Marcos families.

“After Marcos took office, differences between the two sides emerged on domestic and foreign policies, especially regarding (Marcos’) pro-US stance, which led to the public rupture of their relationship,” she said.

This also shows the “fragility of political alliances” in the Philippines, she added.

Malindog-Uy said the power struggle between political dynasties often takes precedence over national governance. When family interests override national interests, Malindog-Uy said this undermines governance and democratic foundation.

data.text:
Ngayong “Araw ng Huwad na Kalayaan,” malinaw ang panawagan ng mamamayang Pilipino: hindi namin kailangan ng mga fighter jet o missiles. Ang kailangan namin ay trabaho, murang pagkain, lupa, at kapayapaan. Panahon na upang wakasan ang presensya ng mga dayuhang sundalo sa ating bansa. Ipanawagan natin ang pagtigil ng lahat ng mga war games, pagtanggal ng mga EDCA site, at agarang pag-alis ng mga tropa at armas ng Estados Unidos mula sa ating teritoryo,” according to Ronnie Manalo, Secretary General of KMP.

Since May, the U.S. military has launched at least three simultaneous joint exercises on Philippine territory:

Kamandag (May 26 to June 6)
Held in Batanes, Capas (Tarlac), Burgos (Ilocos Norte), Palawan, and Tawi-Tawi. Featured the use of HIMARS and NMESIS, including the ROGUE Fires Carrier, an unmanned vehicle armed with Naval Strike Missiles. Involved 2,031 U.S. Marines and 2,028 Philippine troops. Military forces from Japan, South Korea, and the UK participated, while France, Canada, Bahrain, Australia, Indonesia, Thailand,and the Netherlands served as observers.

Kasangga (May 19 to June 24)
Launched at the 4th Infantry Division camp in Cagayan de Oro, now ongoing in Camp Kibaritan, Kalilangan, Bukidnon. Involves 90 Australian and 140 Philippine soldiers.

Salaknib Phase 2 (May 19 to July 20)
Ongoing in Northern Luzon, aimed at strengthening operational integration between the U.S. and Philippine Army units.

KMP lambasted these war exercises that are aimed at preparing Philippine territory and the people for combat roles in a U.S.-China proxy war.

“Farmers outrightly reject the lie that these war games are for the protection of our national security. These war exercises violate our national sovereignty and turn our lands and waters into battlegrounds. Farmers and fisherfolk are displaced by field exercises and artillery fire; rural communities live in fear of surveillance, encampment, and forced evacuation.These military operations disrupt livelihood and heighten tensions that could trigger real conflict,” Manalo concluded.
